title: EPILEPSY, FAMILIAL ADULT MYOCLONIC, 2
alt_titles: CORTICAL MYOCLONIC TREMOR WITH EPILEPSY, FAMILIAL, 2
CORTICAL MYOCLONUS AND EPILEPSY, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that familial adult myoclonic epilepsy-2 (FAME2) is caused by heterozygous expansion of an intronic pentanucleotide (ATTTC) repeat in the STARD7 gene on chromosome 2q11.

checks.claim: Familial adult myoclonic epilepsy-2 (FAME2) is caused by heterozygous expansion of an intronic ATTTC pentanucleotide repeat in the STARD7 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we provide evidence that chr2-linked FAME (FAME2) is caused by an expansion of an ATTTC pentamer within the first intron of STARD7.
checks.explanation: The cause and location are stated, but the paper never says the expansion is heterozygous.

checks.claim: The STARD7 gene is located on chromosome 2q11.
checks.evidence_quote: This revealed an expansion of an ATTTT repeat and insertion of an ATTTC repeat in the context of the reverse strand of chr2 within the first intron of STARD7
checks.explanation: STARD7 lies in the chr2 FAME2 interval (2p11.2-q11.2) at chr2:96.86 Mb. 2q11 is standard location nomenclature restating this.

paragraphs.text: Familial adult myoclonic epilepsy-2 (FAME2) is an autosomal dominant disorder. Its main features are cortical tremor, a fine, rhythmic, irregular myoclonic tremor that mostly affects the hands, and infrequent seizures, which are usually generalized tonic-clonic. Onset is typically in adolescence or adulthood. Electrophysiologic studies show features of cortical reflex myoclonus. These include giant somatosensory evoked potentials, an enhanced long-loop (C) reflex, and a cortical correlate preceding the myoclonic jerks on back-averaging. The course is generally benign.

checks.claim: FAME2 is an autosomal dominant disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: The pattern of inheritance was autosomal dominant with high penetrance.
checks.explanation: The abstract states autosomal dominant inheritance for the family.

checks.claim: A main feature of FAME2 is cortical tremor, a fine, rhythmic, irregular myoclonic tremor that mostly affects the hands.
checks.evidence_quote: predominantly distal, semi-continuous rhythmic myoclonus (all patients)
checks.explanation: The abstract describes distal rhythmic myoclonus. It does not call it 'cortical tremor', describe it as fine or irregular, or say it mostly affects the hands.

checks.claim: A main feature of FAME2 is infrequent seizures, which are usually generalized tonic-clonic.
checks.evidence_quote: generalized tonic-clonic seizures (all patients) and complex partial seizures (three patients). Most individuals had rarely suffered seizures
checks.explanation: Seizures were rare in most patients, and every patient had generalized tonic-clonic seizures.

checks.claim: Onset of FAME2 is typically in adolescence or adulthood.
checks.evidence_quote: a non-progressive disorder with onset between the ages of 12 and 50 years
checks.explanation: Onset between ages 12 and 50 covers adolescence and adulthood.

checks.claim: Electrophysiologic studies in FAME2 show features of cortical reflex myoclonus.
checks.evidence_quote: Electrophysiological study confirmed the presence of cortical reflex myoclonus in all affected members.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Electrophysiologic studies in FAME2 show giant somatosensory evoked potentials.
checks.evidence_quote: somatosensory and visual evoked potentials were of high amplitude
checks.explanation: High-amplitude somatosensory evoked potentials are giant SEPs.

checks.claim: Electrophysiologic studies in FAME2 show an enhanced long-loop (C) reflex.
checks.evidence_quote: The C-reflex at rest was enhanced
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Back-averaging in FAME2 shows a cortical correlate preceding the myoclonic jerks.
checks.evidence_quote: premyoclonus spike detected by means of the jerk-locked averaging EEG method
checks.explanation: A premyoclonus spike found by jerk-locked averaging is a cortical correlate that precedes the jerks.

checks.claim: The course of FAME2 is generally benign.
checks.evidence_quote: infrequent epileptic seizures, nonprogressive course
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the course as nonprogressive, and the related condition is named benign adult familial myoclonic epilepsy.

paragraphs.text: Guerrini et al. (2001) described a large Italian family with an autosomal dominant syndrome that they called autosomal dominant cortical myoclonus and epilepsy (ADCME). Affected members had cortical myoclonic tremor of adult onset and seizures. The seizures included generalized tonic-clonic seizures, and some affected members also had focal seizures. Neurophysiologic studies showed that the myoclonus originated in the cortex.

checks.claim: Guerrini et al. (2001) described a large Italian family with an autosomal dominant syndrome they called autosomal dominant cortical myoclonus and epilepsy (ADCME).
checks.evidence_quote: The pattern of inheritance was autosomal dominant with high penetrance. We defined this disorder as autosomal dominant cortical myoclonus and epilepsy (ADCME).
checks.explanation: The abstract supports the autosomal dominant inheritance and the ADCME name. It does not say the family was Italian or describe it as large; it mentions only a pedigree with eight affected individuals. These details are not in the abstract supplied.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Italian ADCME family had cortical myoclonic tremor of adult onset.
checks.evidence_quote: onset between the ages of 12 and 50 years. It was characterized by predominantly distal, semi-continuous rhythmic myoclonus (all patients)
checks.explanation: Onset ranged from age 12 to 50, which includes adolescence, so 'adult onset' is only roughly right. The abstract says 'myoclonus', not 'tremor'.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Italian ADCME family had seizures, including generalized tonic-clonic seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: generalized tonic-clonic seizures (all patients)
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Some affected members of the Italian ADCME family had focal seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: complex partial seizures (three patients)
checks.explanation: Complex partial seizures are focal seizures.

checks.claim: Neurophysiologic studies in the Italian ADCME family showed that the myoclonus originated in the cortex.
checks.evidence_quote: A neurophysiological study of the myoclonus suggested a cortical origin.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: De Falco et al. (2003) studied Italian families with benign adult familial myoclonic epilepsy (BAFME). Affected members had distal cortical myoclonic tremor and rare generalized seizures, with electrophysiologic signs of cortical reflex myoclonus.

checks.claim: De Falco et al. (2003) studied Italian families with benign adult familial myoclonic epilepsy (BAFME).
checks.evidence_quote: The authors report a clinical and electrophysiologic study of two Italian BAFME families showing linkage to chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the study was of two Italian BAFME families.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Italian BAFME families studied by de Falco et al. (2003) had distal cortical myoclonic tremor.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not describe the patients' symptoms. Details of the myoclonic tremor would be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Italian BAFME families studied by de Falco et al. (2003) had rare generalized seizures.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not describe seizures in these families.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Italian BAFME families studied by de Falco et al. (2003) had electrophysiologic signs of cortical reflex myoclonus.
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions an electrophysiologic study but does not report its findings.

paragraphs.text: The families reported by Guerrini et al. (2001) and de Falco et al. (2003) showed autosomal dominant inheritance of FAME2.

checks.claim: The Italian ADCME family reported by Guerrini et al. (2001) showed autosomal dominant inheritance of FAME2.
checks.evidence_quote: The pattern of inheritance was autosomal dominant with high penetrance.
checks.explanation: Autosomal dominant inheritance is stated. The abstract does not mention that the family was Italian.

checks.claim: The Italian BAFME families reported by de Falco et al. (2003) showed autosomal dominant inheritance of FAME2.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not state the inheritance pattern in these families.

paragraphs.text: In the Italian family with ADCME, Guerrini et al. (2001) found linkage to the pericentromeric region of chromosome 2, at 2p11.1-q12.2.

checks.claim: Guerrini et al. (2001) found linkage of ADCME in the Italian family to the pericentromeric region of chromosome 2, at 2p11.1-q12.2.
checks.evidence_quote: Genome-wide linkage analysis identified a critical region spanning 12.4 cM between markers D2S2161 and D2S1897 in 2p11.1-q12.2
checks.explanation: The abstract also localizes the gene to the centromeric region of chromosome 2.

paragraphs.text: De Falco et al. (2003) found linkage to the same region on chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2 in Italian families with BAFME. This region is distinct from the FAME1 locus on chromosome 8q.

checks.claim: De Falco et al. (2003) found linkage of BAFME in Italian families to chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2, the same region identified for ADCME.
checks.evidence_quote: two Italian BAFME families showing linkage to chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2. Their report supports the evidence of non-Japanese families with BAFME and suggests a possible allelism with the recently described autosomal dominant cortical myoclonus and epilepsy syndrome.
checks.explanation: Linkage to 2p11.1-q12.2 is stated. The abstract only suggests possible allelism with ADCME and does not say outright that ADCME maps to the same region.

checks.claim: The BAFME locus on chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2 is distinct from the FAME1 locus on chromosome 8q.
checks.evidence_quote: Benign adult familial myoclonic epilepsy (BAFME) has been mapped to chromosome 8q24; however, genetic heterogeneity has been recently suggested.
checks.explanation: The new 2p locus is presented as different from the earlier 8q24 locus (FAME1).

paragraphs.text: Madia et al. (2008) studied 5 Italian families with BAFME linked to chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2. They found a shared extended haplotype, which suggested a founder effect, and the shared region narrowed the candidate interval.

checks.claim: Madia et al. (2008) studied 5 Italian families with BAFME linked to chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2.
checks.evidence_quote: Significant linkage was found on chromosome 2p11.1-q12.2 and a maximum cumulative lod score of 18.5 was found for markers D2S2161 and D2S388.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports five Italian BAFME families linked to 2p11.1-q12.2.

checks.claim: Madia et al. (2008) found a shared extended haplotype in the 5 Italian BAFME families, suggesting a founder effect.
checks.evidence_quote: The haplotype "5332" of adjacent markers D2S388, D2S2216, D2S113, and D2S2175 segregates with the disease in all families indicating that the same mutation inherited from a common ancestor segregates in these families.
checks.explanation: A shared founder haplotype is reported. The title also calls it an 'extended founder haplotype'.

checks.claim: The shared haplotype region in the 5 Italian BAFME families narrowed the chromosome 2 candidate interval.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not say the shared haplotype narrowed the candidate interval.

paragraphs.text: Familial adult myoclonic epilepsy is genetically heterogeneous. Other loci have been mapped to chromosomes 8q, 5p, and 3q. At several of these loci, the cause has been shown to be intronic pentanucleotide repeat expansions in different genes.

checks.claim: Familial adult myoclonic epilepsy is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: Exclusion of linkage of this family to the locus for familial adult myoclonic epilepsy/benign adult familial myoclonic epilepsy established the genetic heterogeneity of this disorder.
checks.explanation: The abstract states directly that the disorder is genetically heterogeneous.

checks.claim: Other familial adult myoclonic epilepsy loci have been mapped to chromosomes 8q, 5p, and 3q.
checks.evidence_quote: Additional pedigrees affected by similar forms of epilepsy have been associated with chromosomes 8q, 5p, and 3q, but none of the causing genes has been identified.
checks.explanation: Loci on 8q, 5p, 3q stated.

checks.claim: At several familial adult myoclonic epilepsy loci, the cause has been shown to be intronic pentanucleotide repeat expansions in different genes.
checks.evidence_quote: The pathogenic ATTTC insertion and expansion was always accompanied by the endogenous ATTTT pentanucleotide repeat in all cases of FAME2 that we describe here, replicating the findings in the cases of FAME with expansions in SAMD12, TNRC6A, RAPGEF2,, and the report of a similar expansion in MARCH6 causing chr5-linked FAME.
checks.explanation: Intronic pentanucleotide repeat expansions are reported in SAMD12 (chr8) and MARCH6 (chr5).

paragraphs.text: Corbett et al. (2019) studied families of European ancestry with FAME linked to chromosome 2. In affected members they identified heterozygous expansion of an ATTTC pentanucleotide repeat inserted within an AAAAT repeat in intron 1 of the STARD7 gene. The expansion segregated with the disorder in the families. The expanded alleles were not found in controls, although normal-length AAAAT repeat alleles were common. The STARD7 transcript was not found to be clearly reduced. Corbett et al. (2019) noted that the same mechanism, expansion of an intronic ATTTC repeat, had been found at other FAME loci. They suggested that the mechanism is independent of the gene in which the expansion lies.

checks.claim: Corbett et al. (2019) studied families of European ancestry with FAME linked to chromosome 2.
checks.evidence_quote: The FAME2 locus is the most frequently observed linked region for Caucasian individuals affected by this disorder
checks.explanation: Most families are European (Australian/NZ, Italian, South African of European ancestry, French/Spanish), but the cohort also includes Iraqi and Israeli Sephardic Jewish families and a Syrian case.

checks.claim: Corbett et al. (2019) identified in affected members heterozygous expansion of an ATTTC pentanucleotide repeat inserted within an AAAAT repeat in intron 1 of the STARD7 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: This suggested the structure of the pathogenic repeat in the context of the forward strand of chr2 was (AAATG)n[N](AAAAT)n, where (n) represents the unknown number of each repeat sequence.
checks.explanation: The paper describes an ATTTC insertion adjacent to the expanded endogenous ATTTT/AAAAT repeat in intron 1, not strictly within it. Heterozygosity is not stated.

checks.claim: The STARD7 intron 1 ATTTC repeat expansion segregated with FAME in the families studied by Corbett et al. (2019).
checks.evidence_quote: The ATTTC expansions segregate in 158/158 individuals typically affected by FAME from 22 pedigrees including 16 previously reported families recruited worldwide.
checks.explanation: The paper reports full segregation with the disorder.

checks.claim: The expanded STARD7 ATTTC repeat alleles were not found in controls.
checks.evidence_quote: The ATTTC repeat expansion did not amplify in any of 28 control DNA samples extracted from unaffected individuals unrelated to FAME.
checks.explanation: The expansion was also absent from the WGS data of 69 controls.

checks.claim: Normal-length AAAAT repeat alleles in STARD7 intron 1 were common in controls.
checks.evidence_quote: The endogenous ATTTT repeat in intron 1 of STARD7 was also found to be variable in length in the normal population but not expanded to the same extent as repeats found in individuals with FAME.
checks.explanation: The paper describes the endogenous repeat as present and variable in the normal population. The AAAAT/ATTTT difference is only strand notation.

checks.claim: The STARD7 transcript was not found to be clearly reduced in carriers of the ATTTC repeat expansion.
checks.evidence_quote: showed no significant differences in STARD7 transcript expression in patient-derived fibroblast cell lines
checks.explanation: qPCR and RNA-Seq showed no change in STARD7 expression.

checks.claim: Corbett et al. (2019) noted that expansion of an intronic ATTTC repeat had been found at other FAME loci.
checks.evidence_quote: These data, in combination with other genes bearing similar mutations that have been implicated in FAME, suggest ATTTC expansions may cause this disorder, irrespective of the genomic locus involved.
checks.explanation: The paper refers to similar expansions in other FAME genes and loci.

checks.claim: Corbett et al. (2019) suggested that the FAME intronic ATTTC repeat expansion mechanism is independent of the gene in which the expansion lies.
checks.evidence_quote: These data suggest the repeat sequence alone is pathogenic, independent of an effect on the coding sequence of the encompassing gene.
checks.explanation: This states the gene-independent mechanism directly.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Cortical myoclonic tremor of the hands
